children: Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures traded flat and feeder cattle weakened on Thursday as market players awaited Friday's US Department of Agriculture Cattle on Feed report.
Meanwhile, weakness in lean hog futures continued for a second session in a row during a period of seasonal weakness, according to analysts.
ended the day unchanged at 231.125 cents per pound.
finished the day down 2.720 cents at 346.10 cents per pound.
The USDA will report the country's cattle on feed inventory as nearly flat from a year ago as of Oct. 1, according to a Reuters poll of analysts late on Wednesday.
Trade analysts estimated that placements of cattle on feed were about 100.3% of last year's numbers at this time.
A stronger cash trade also added support, according StoneX in a client note.

Wholesale boxed beef prices fell at midday on Thursday to $369.47 per hundredweight (cwt) for choice cuts, down $3.12 from a day earlier, the US Department of Agriculture said. Select cuts fell $4.93 to $350.41 per cwt.

Beef packer margins widened. The average margin on Wednesday was estimated at $32.15 per head, down from $50.15 on Wednesday, and $99.65 a week ago, according to livestock marketing advisory service HedgersEdge.
A seasonal fall in hog demand is expected during this time of year, said StoneX, but the weakness in the pork cut out and cash market is notable.
The USDA reported wholesale hog carcasses were priced at $75.23 per cwt on Thursday afternoon, up $0.73 from the previous day.
Pork bellies were reported at $84.59 per cwt, up $6.93 from Wednesday.
December lean hogs (LHZ26) ended 0.175 cent lower at 65.55 cents per pound, having hit a contract low of 65.05 cents per pound earlier in the session.
